name: Mina
about: Mina is Persian for enamel, while minakari is the craft of decorating metal with it. This diverging palette comes from a lidded minakari vessel. Copper and rose meet at an enamel-white center, then turn toward pale blue, turquoise, cobalt and indigo. The blue side dominates, just as it does on the piece.
craft: Mina is the enamel itself, a heat-fused glass paste colored by metal oxides. Minakari means enamelwork, the craft of decorating metal with that enamel. Persian makers have used the medium for vessels and boxes, often with floral designs, fine detail, royal blue, turquoise and pink.
notes: deep claret, the darkest red flower strokes
copper red, outlines around the body panels
dusty rose, sunlit edges of the copper outlines
pale sky, blue-white highlights in the panels
clear blue, the broad painted leaves and petals
turquoise, small leaf strokes across the white ground
cobalt, the main arabesques and blue bands
indigo, the deepest outlines and shaded blue enamel
